newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa aims for 1997 profit lift.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa aims for 1997 profit lift.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG, seeking to rebound from a 1996 slump, said Wednesday it was on course for markedly higher 1997 profits after posting a first-quarter profit for the first time.

"The year has started well for Lufthansa. If we manage to maintain the momentum of the first quarter, we ought to succeed in generating a markedly higher profit in 1997 than in 1996," Chief Financial Officer Klaus Schlede said in a statement.
Lufthansa said pre-tax earnings for the first quarter were 20 million German marks ($11.6 million) vs. a 1996 first quarter loss of 49 million marks ($28.5 million).

"The first quarter has ended in profit for the first time in the airline's history. In our part of the world, it is normally a loss-maker," said Lufthansa Chief Executive Juergen Weber at the news conference.

Lufthansa had an operating loss of 1 million marks ($581,000) compared with a 49 million mark ($28.5 million) loss last year, but financial operations, which includes income from subsidiaries and associated companies, pushed the airline into profit.
Revenues in the first three months climbed 8.5 percent to almost 5 billion marks ($2.9 billion), with 90 percent of the sales coming from passenger and freight services.
The balance of the group's revenues came from Lufthansa's aero-engineering services and its LSG catering business, raising the group's total sales to 5.28 billion marks ($3.1 billion).
